papers_read.title_as_printed: Statistical Method for Identification of Alzheimer Disease With Multimodal Predictive Markers Mild Cognitive Impairment (Zarei, Shalbaf & Shalbaf, Basic and Clinical Neuroscience 2025, 16(SI):233-250)
Prediction of progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease with longitudinal and multimodal data (Ding et al., Frontiers in Dementia 2023)

what_each_reports.P-334: ADNI-MERGE, 835 MCI participants (487 sMCI, 348 pMCI), labels applied to individual visit records (pMCI records only within 3 years before conversion). Univariate AUC per single feature, no multivariable model and no validation: florbetaben PET (FBB) AUC 0.84 (highest), mPACCtrailsB and ADAS13 0.83, hippocampus 0.75, FDG 0.75.
what_each_reports.P-168: ADNI-MERGE, 347 participants with MCI at the 24-month exam (77 converters). LSTM on demographics + 15 NP tests + 7 FreeSurfer MRI volumes at five time points (baseline to 24 months), predicting conversion to AD within 2 years of the index exam, 10-fold CV: AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06; single-time-point random forest 0.90; MRI-only LSTM 0.86; NP-only LSTM 0.89.

quantity_a: Univariate record-level ROC-AUC of a single amyloid-PET measure (florbetaben SUVR) for separating stable-MCI visit records from pMCI visit records within 3 years before conversion; no model, no validation
quantity_b: Cross-validated participant-level ROC-AUC of a multivariable longitudinal model (five visits of NP tests + structural MRI volumes + demographics) for conversion from MCI to AD within 2 years of the index exam
incompatible_if_same: No: a single biomarker's univariate AUC of 0.84 and a multivariable model's AUC of 0.93 (+/- 0.06) do not contradict each other; P-168's own single-modality figures (0.86 MRI, 0.89 NP) sit near P-334's single-feature values (0.83 for mPACCtrailsB/ADAS13).

gates.task: match: both MCI-to-AD progression (T2), though horizons differ (records within 3 years of conversion vs conversion within 2 years of index exam)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (ADNI-MERGE); overlapping participants likely
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-334 fits no model and validates nothing (descriptive univariate AUCs); P-168 uses 10-fold CV
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-334's contested 0.84 is amyloid PET (florbetaben); P-168 uses structural MRI volumes + neuropsychological tests, no PET; the record itself has modality_family_equal 'No'

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both ROC-AUC, but univariate single-marker record-level discrimination vs multivariable longitudinal participant-level prediction, with different horizons
performance_validity: flag does not apply (both < 0.97); P-334 is not a validated classifier at all
independence: Distinct author groups; both draw on ADNI-MERGE, so participant overlap is probable (recorded as non-independence)
grounds: P-334's 0.84 is the univariate AUC of a single florbetaben PET measure, while P-168's 0.93 is a cross-validated multivariable LSTM on repeated NP tests and MRI volumes, so predictor set and input modality differ.

P-334 labels individual visit records within a 3-year pre-conversion window and fits no model, while P-168 predicts participant-level conversion within 2 years, so the endpoint definitions and validation tier differ.
The modality gate fails (amyloid PET vs structural MRI + cognition) with no waiver on record, and on comparable single-modality figures the two papers are close rather than contradictory.

evidence_quotes.quote: Our findings showed the strong predictive potential of PET, particularly florbetaben (FBB), which achieved an AUC of 0.84.
Only records preceding the AD diagnosis and those within the 3-year window before the conversion event receive labels.
Employing the Wilcoxon test (Wilcoxon, 1992) in R version 4, we scrutinized differences in the AUC, setting a stringent significance level (alpha) at 0.005.
The longitudinal LSTM model showed superior prediction performance of MCI-to-AD progression (AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06) compared to the random forest model (AUC 0.90 +/- 0.09).
The LSTM model utilizing longitudinal data reached the best performance, comparing to an AUC of 0.86 when using MRI measures.

record_defects: task_equal/dataset_equal/validation_comparable 'Yes': validation is not comparable, since P-334 fits no model.
P-334 registry Sample_N_Approx '487' is the sMCI group only; the analysed total is 835 (487 sMCI + 348 pMCI).
P-334 registry Modality 'MRI/PET' hides that the contested 0.84 is a PET-only single feature; P-168 uses no PET.
resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (AUC)' while the resolution field says 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch'; the two fields contradict each other.
what_would_change_the_verdict: P-334 reporting a validated multivariable model on the same NP + MRI inputs and 2-year horizon, or P-168 reporting a single-feature AUC that conflicted with P-334's.
